_note: Every state the project covers. Scripts, the site build and the skills read this list; adding a state starts here (see the odc-add-state skill).

water_agency.name: Louisiana Department of Energy and Natural Resources

records_law.name: Louisiana Public Records Law
records_law.deadline: 3 business days

water_agency.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality, Office of Land and Water

records_law.name: Mississippi Public Records Act of 1983
records_law.deadline: 7 working days

states.name: Virginia

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Virginia

water_agency.name: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Water Withdrawal Permitting

records_law.name: Virginia Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 5 working days
records_law.who_can_ask: citizens of Virginia, plus representatives of newspapers and magazines circulated in Virginia and of radio and TV stations broadcasting in or into Virginia

states.county_note: Virginia has 95 counties and 38 independent cities that sit outside any county; treat each independent city as a county-level unit.

states.name: Maryland

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Maryland

water_agency.name: Maryland Department of the Environment, Water and Science Administration (water appropriation permits)

records_law.name: Maryland Public Information Act
records_law.cite: Md. Code Ann., Gen. Provisions § 4-101 et seq.
records_law.deadline: promptly, but not more than 30 days after receiving the application (a custodian expecting to take longer than 10 working days must say so within 10 working days)

states.county_note: Maryland has 23 counties plus Baltimore city, an independent city that is its own county-level unit.

states.name: District of Columbia

economic_development.name: Deputy Mayor for Planning and Economic Development

utility_regulator.name: Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia

environment_agency.name: District Department of Energy and Environment

water_agency.name: District Department of Energy and Environment

legislature.name: Council of the District of Columbia

revenue.name: DC Office of Tax and Revenue

records_law.name: District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 15 days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays)

states.county_note: DC has no counties; the District is one unit, so treat the whole District as a single county-level entry (Census county FIPS 001).

states.name: Delaware

economic_development.name: Delaware Division of Small Business (Choose Delaware)

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Delaware

environment_agency.name: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control

water_agency.name: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control, Water Supply (water allocation permits)

records_law.name: Delaware Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: as soon as possible, but in any event within 15 business days

states.county_note: Delaware has only three counties: New Castle, Kent and Sussex.

states.name: West Virginia

economic_development.name: West Virginia Department of Economic Development

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of West Virginia

utility_regulator.name: Public Service Commission of West Virginia

environment_agency.name: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection

water_agency.name: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection, Division of Water and Waste Management

records_law.name: West Virginia Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: as soon as is practicable but within a maximum of five days not including Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays

states.county_note: West Virginia has 55 counties and no independent cities.

economic_development.name: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Pennsylvania

water_agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (water withdrawals; the Susquehanna and Delaware River Basin Commissions also approve withdrawals in their basins)

records_law.name: Pennsylvania Right-to-Know Law
records_law.deadline: 5 business days
records_law.who_can_ask: a legal resident of the United States

economic_development.name: Economic Development Partnership of North Carolina

environment_agency.name: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality

water_agency.name: North Carolina DEQ, Division of Water Resources

records_law.name: North Carolina Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: as promptly as possible

environment_agency.name: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services

water_agency.name: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services

records_law.name: South Carolina Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 10 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, to notify the requester of the decision (20 such days if the record is more than 24 months old)
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (except people serving a prison sentence)

states.name: Georgia

water_agency.name: Georgia Environmental Protection Division

records_law.name: Georgia Open Records Act
records_law.deadline: a reasonable amount of time not to exceed 3 business days
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (no residency requirement per Georgia Attorney General Op. 93-27)

states.county_note: Georgia has 159 counties, and several consolidated governments (Athens-Clarke, Augusta-Richmond, Columbus-Muscogee, Macon-Bibb, Cusseta-Chattahoochee, Georgetown-Quitman, Webster, Statenville-Echols) act as both city and county.

states.name: Florida

water_agency.name: Florida Water Management Districts (consumptive use permits), via DEP

records_law.name: Florida Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: must acknowledge requests promptly and respond in good faith (no fixed number of days)

states.county_note: Florida has 67 counties. Jacksonville-Duval is a consolidated city-county. Water use permits come from five regional water management districts, not one state agency.

states.name: Tennessee

economic_development.name: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development

environment_agency.name: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation

water_agency.name: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of Water Resources

records_law.name: Tennessee Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: promptly; if not practicable, within 7 business days to grant, deny in writing, or give a time estimate
records_law.who_can_ask: citizens of Tennessee (ID may be required)

states.county_note: Nashville-Davidson, Lynchburg-Moore and Hartsville-Trousdale are consolidated city-county governments. Much of the grid is run by the federal TVA through local power companies, not the state utility commission.

states.name: Kentucky

water_agency.name: Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet, Division of Water

records_law.name: Kentucky Open Records Act
records_law.deadline: 3 business days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays) to respond in writing
records_law.who_can_ask: any Kentucky resident, as defined in KRS 61.870 (includes people who work in Kentucky, own property there, and news organizations)

states.county_note: Louisville-Jefferson County and Lexington-Fayette are merged city-county governments.

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Alabama

water_agency.name: Alabama Office of Water Resources (ADECA)

records_law.name: Alabama Open Records Act (Public Records Law)
records_law.deadline: Acknowledge within 10 days; substantive response within 15 business days of acknowledging (standard request); 45 business days for time-intensive requests
records_law.deadline_cite: Ala. Code § 36-12-44 (added by SB 270, 2024, effective Oct. 1, 2024)
records_law.who_can_ask: any resident (an individual permanently domiciled in Alabama, shown by reasonable proof of residency)

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Arkansas

water_agency.name: Arkansas Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Division

revenue.name: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

records_law.name: Arkansas Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: Available immediately; if a record is in active use or storage, the custodian must certify that in writing and set a date and hour within 3 working days
records_law.who_can_ask: any citizen of the State of Arkansas

states.name: Texas

economic_development.name: Office of the Governor, Economic Development and Tourism

water_agency.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (surface water rights)

records_law.name: Texas Public Information Act
records_law.deadline: Promptly (as soon as possible under the circumstances, within a reasonable time, without delay); if not producible within 10 business days, the officer must certify that in writing and set a date and hour within a reasonable time

states.county_note: Texas has 254 counties, the most of any state; groundwater is managed by local groundwater conservation districts, not the state.

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Oklahoma

water_agency.name: Oklahoma Water Resources Board

records_law.name: Oklahoma Open Records Act
records_law.deadline: Prompt, reasonable access during regular business hours (no fixed number of days)

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of New Mexico

water_agency.name: New Mexico Office of the State Engineer

revenue.name: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department

records_law.name: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act (IPRA)
records_law.deadline: Immediately or as soon as practicable, no later than 15 calendar days; if not permitted within 3 business days, written explanation of when records will be available

water_agency.name: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Water Resources

records_law.name: Ohio Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: promptly (records "promptly prepared and made available"; copies "within a reasonable period of time")

water_agency.name: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Water

records_law.name: Indiana Access to Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 7 days to respond to a mailed or faxed request; the law sets no deadline for producing the records (a reasonable time, per Public Access Counselor opinions)

economic_development.name: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity

water_agency.name: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, Office of Water Resources

records_law.name: Illinois Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 5 business days (one 5-business-day extension allowed for listed reasons)

environment_agency.name: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy

water_agency.name: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy, Water Resources Division

records_law.name: Michigan Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 5 business days (one extension of up to 10 business days allowed)
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (except a person serving a sentence in a state or local correctional facility)

water_agency.name: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Water Use Program

records_law.name: Wisconsin Public Records Law
records_law.deadline: as soon as practicable and without delay
records_law.who_can_ask: any requester (an incarcerated person has narrower rights)

economic_development.name: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development

governor_news.name: Office of Governor Tim Walz and Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan

water_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (water appropriation permits)

records_law.name: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act
records_law.deadline: no fixed number of days; entities must respond in an "appropriate and prompt manner"; copies "as soon as reasonably possible"

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Iowa

water_agency.name: Iowa Department of Natural Resources (water use permits)

records_law.name: Iowa Open Records Law
records_law.deadline: no fixed number of days; any delay must be good-faith and reasonable. Delay to decide whether a confidential record can be released may not exceed 20 calendar days and ordinarily should not exceed 10 business days

states.name: Missouri

water_agency.name: Missouri Department of Natural Resources (Water Resources Center)

records_law.name: Missouri Sunshine Law
records_law.cite: Mo. Rev. Stat. ch. 610 (§ 610.010 et seq.)
records_law.deadline: 3 business days

states.county_note: St. Louis city is an independent city that belongs to no county, and St. Louis County is a separate county. Kansas City spans parts of Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties.

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Kansas

environment_agency.name: Kansas Department of Health and Environment

water_agency.name: Kansas Department of Agriculture, Division of Water Resources

records_law.name: Kansas Open Records Act
records_law.deadline: 3 business days

governor_news.name: Office of the Governor of Nebraska

environment_agency.name: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment

water_agency.name: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment

records_law.name: Nebraska Public Records Statutes
records_law.deadline: 4 business days
records_law.who_can_ask: citizens of Nebraska and other persons interested in examining the records

environment_agency.name: North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality

water_agency.name: North Dakota Department of Water Resources (State Engineer)

revenue.name: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner

records_law.name: North Dakota Open Records Law
records_law.deadline: no fixed number of days; the law says a record may not be "unreasonably delayed"
records_law.who_can_ask: anyone; the agency may not ask who you are or why you want the records (§ 44-04-18(2))

economic_development.name: South Dakota Governor's Office of Economic Development

environment_agency.name: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources

water_agency.name: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Water Rights Program

records_law.name: South Dakota Open Records Law
records_law.deadline: 10 business days for a written request (a records officer may instead acknowledge and estimate more time); silence past 10 days is treated as a denial
records_law.who_can_ask: any citizen of the state and any other person interested in the records (SDCL 1-27-1)

states.name: Montana

water_agency.name: Montana Department of Natural Resources and Conservation

records_law.name: Montana Right to Know and Public Records law
records_law.cite: Mont. Const. art. II, § 9; MCA § 2-6-1001 et seq.
records_law.deadline: State agencies: acknowledge within 5 business days, and a single readily available record within 5 working days of acknowledgment. Local governments: respond "in a timely manner" (no fixed number of days)

states.county_note: Montana has two consolidated city-counties, Anaconda-Deer Lodge County and Butte-Silver Bow, in addition to its other counties.

water_agency.name: Wyoming State Engineer's Office

records_law.name: Wyoming Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: not later than 30 calendar days from acknowledged receipt (released immediately if readily available; 7 business days to say if records are in storage or held by another body); a later date needs good cause

states.name: Colorado

economic_development.name: Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade

environment_agency.name: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment

water_agency.name: Colorado Division of Water Resources (State Engineer)

revenue.name: Colorado Department of Revenue, Taxation Division

records_law.name: Colorado Open Records Act (CORA)
records_law.deadline: 3 working days (the presumed reasonable time), extendable by up to 7 more working days with a written finding of extenuating circumstances
records_law.who_can_ask: any person; the custodian may not require ID (C.R.S. § 24-72-203(1)(a))

states.county_note: Denver and Broomfield are consolidated city-counties.

economic_development.name: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity

water_agency.name: Utah Division of Water Rights

records_law.name: Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA)
records_law.deadline: as soon as reasonably possible, no more than 10 business days (5 business days for an approved expedited request, such as from media)

water_agency.name: Arizona Department of Water Resources

records_law.name: Arizona Public Records Law
records_law.deadline: promptly

states.name: Nevada

water_agency.name: Nevada Division of Water Resources

records_law.name: Nevada Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 5 business days

states.county_note: Carson City is an independent consolidated municipality that works as a county; Nevada has 16 counties plus Carson City.

states.name: California

economic_development.name: Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

water_agency.name: State Water Resources Control Board (Division of Water Rights)

revenue.name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration

records_law.name: California Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 10 days to decide whether records are disclosable

states.county_note: San Francisco is a consolidated city and county.

water_agency.name: Oregon Water Resources Department

records_law.name: Oregon Public Records Law
records_law.deadline: acknowledge within 5 business days; finish within 10 business days after that

water_agency.name: Washington State Department of Ecology, Water Resources Program

records_law.name: Washington Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 5 business days to respond

water_agency.name: Idaho Department of Water Resources

records_law.name: Idaho Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 3 working days for a resident (21 days for a non-resident); up to 10 working days (35 days non-resident) if the agency says in writing it needs longer
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (Idaho Code § 74-102(1)); request must go to the agency's designated custodian and clearly say it is a public records request

states.name: Alaska

economic_development.name: Alaska Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

water_agency.name: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Mining, Land and Water

states.county_note: Alaska has no counties: it has 19 organized boroughs (including consolidated city-boroughs such as Anchorage and Juneau) and the Unorganized Borough, which the Census splits into census areas.

records_law.name: Alaska Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 10 working days for an initial response from state executive-branch agencies (one extension of up to 10 more working days with written notice); the statute itself sets no number of days
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (AS 40.25.120(a): "Every person has a right to inspect a public record in the state")

states.name: Hawaii

economic_development.name: Hawaii Department of Business, Economic Development and Tourism

environment_agency.name: Hawaii Department of Health, Environmental Health Administration

water_agency.name: Hawaii Commission on Water Resource Management (DLNR)

states.county_note: Hawaii has four main counties (Hawaii, Honolulu, Kauai, Maui); Honolulu is a consolidated city and county covering all of Oahu. Kalawao County is a tiny Census county run by the state Department of Health.

records_law.name: Uniform Information Practices Act (Modified)
records_law.deadline: 10 business days (to disclose a fully public record, or to send a written notice for other records); up to 20 business days for the notice if the agency sends an acknowledgment within 10 business days citing extenuating circumstances

utility_regulator.name: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities

environment_agency.name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

water_agency.name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection, Division of Water Supply and Geoscience

records_law.name: Open Public Records Act (OPRA)
records_law.deadline: 7 business days (14 business days for commercial-purpose requests)
records_law.who_can_ask: any person (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a)); since Sept. 3, 2024 the request form must include the certifications in 47:1A-5(f) and (g)

states.name: New York

utility_regulator.name: New York State Department of Public Service (Public Service Commission)

environment_agency.name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

water_agency.name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, Division of Water

revenue.name: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance

states.county_note: New York City's five boroughs are each a county (Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens, Richmond).

records_law.name: Freedom of Information Law (FOIL)
records_law.deadline: 5 business days to grant, deny, or acknowledge in writing with an approximate date; if more time is needed, a decision within 20 business days of the acknowledgment (or a written reason and a date certain)

states.name: Connecticut

economic_development.name: Connecticut Department of Economic and Community Development

environment_agency.name: Department of Energy and Environmental Protection

water_agency.name: Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (water diversion permits)

records_law.name: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act
records_law.deadline: 4 business days to deny in writing; otherwise records must be provided promptly

states.county_note: Connecticut abolished county government in 1960. Counties survive only as old Census units, and the state now uses 9 planning regions (since 2022) in their place; local government is by 169 towns.

states.name: Rhode Island

environment_agency.name: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

water_agency.name: Rhode Island Water Resources Board

records_law.name: Access to Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 10 business days (may extend by 20 more business days for good cause)

states.county_note: Rhode Island has 5 counties, but they have no county government. Its 39 cities and towns do the local work.

states.name: Massachusetts

economic_development.name: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

water_agency.name: MassDEP Water Management Act Program

records_law.name: Massachusetts Public Records Law
records_law.deadline: 10 business days

states.county_note: Several Massachusetts counties (such as Middlesex and Worcester) were abolished as governments and their duties moved to the state; others still run limited services. Cities and towns hold most local power.

states.name: Vermont

economic_development.name: Vermont Agency of Commerce and Community Development

environment_agency.name: Vermont Agency of Natural Resources, Department of Environmental Conservation

water_agency.name: Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation (water programs)

records_law.name: Vermont Public Records Act
records_law.deadline: 3 business days (may extend up to 10 business days by written notice in unusual circumstances)

states.county_note: Vermont has 14 counties, but they have little government role; towns and cities run local affairs. Counties mainly hold courts and sheriffs.

economic_development.name: New Hampshire Division of Economic Development

environment_agency.name: New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services

water_agency.name: New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services (water)

revenue.name: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration

records_law.name: Right-to-Know Law
records_law.deadline: 5 business days to produce, deny in writing, or acknowledge with a time estimate
records_law.who_can_ask: every citizen (RSA 91-A:4, I); the statute does not define citizen

economic_development.name: Maine Department of Economic and Community Development

water_agency.name: Maine Department of Environmental Protection (water and land permits)

records_law.name: Freedom of Access Act
records_law.deadline: Acknowledge within 5 working days; then respond within a reasonable time (good-faith estimate); written denial within 5 working days
